messages:
Alex W: Heads up — customer corp-ventus (on-prem) flagged a ~3% token delta between their internal audit and our billing ledger for the 2026-02-09 window. They say totals on their audit CSV vs invoices differ by ~18k tokens.
Priya S: Oof. Any obvious errors in the agent heartbeat or disk I/O?
meter-agent-bot: automated alert: agent-ventus-03 reported `ack_ttl_expiry` events during GC window (2026-02-09T03:12:xxZ -> 03:18:xxZ). Count=12
Alex W: I grabbed the agent logs during the window — looks like a backlog flush after a short disk remount. Logs show a burst of offline buffering and then a replay with some seq gaps.
Kevin M: Can you paste the minimal repro/log snippet? Also we need the seq ranges and any retry IDs.
Alex W: snippet below (redacted):
```
[2026-02-09T03:11:58Z] INFO  meter-agent  flush queued=0 -> buffering=1
[2026-02-09T03:12:03Z] WARN  meter-agent  disk remounted, paused ingestion
[2026-02-09T03:13:41Z] INFO  meter-agent  replay start seq=1422334
[2026-02-09T03:14:04Z] ERROR meter-agent  missing seq range seq=1422340-1422343 (seq-unreachable)
[2026-02-09T03:15:10Z] INFO  meter-agent  replay complete seq=1422349
[2026-02-09T03:15:10Z] INFO  meter-agent  acked tokens=182310
[2026-02-09T03:15:11Z] WARN  meter-agent  ack_ttl_expiry id=abc123
```
Priya S: That missing seq range is suspicious — could be trimmed by retention or lost during offline buffer handoff. Do we have the agent's local ledger snapshot?
Alex W: Customer provided `ledger.db` hash and short export — they have entries for 1422334..1422349 but our central ingestion only shows 1422334..1422339 and 1422344..1422349. So 1422340-43 never made it to central.
Kevin M: Two hypotheses: 1) agent replay skipped those because a TTL ack expired and agent dropped those events on cleanup, or 2) central ingestion rejected duplicates due to bad checksums during remount resulting in silent drop. Need to check broker ingest logs for that exact seq window.
Lisa B: For billing reconciliation, what's the delta amount (tokens)? I need a ballpark to advise finance before they escalate.
Alex W: From agent ack counts vs central ledger it's about 18,240 tokens. Customer reported 18,000 so matches.
Priya S: Steps to reproduce / validate on our side: 1) fetch raw events from agent export for 1422338..1422346; 2) check broker-ingest logs for t=03:13..03:15 for any `checksum-mismatch` or `duplicate-suppressed` entries; 3) check remount timeline to confirm if agent rewrote inode timestamps causing TTL mismatch.
Kevin M: I'll pull broker logs and search for `seq=1422340` and `checksum` flags. Also will grep for `ack_ttl_expiry` and correlate with node time offset. If node clock jumped >30s, TTL calc can expire pending ack before central persists.
Alex W: Customer says they had a planned maintenance that touched NFS mounts at 03:12. That would explain disk pause. They also said VM time was NTP synced but we should still check step events.
Lisa B: If we confirm a server-side ingestion drop, finance will need a credit memo for 18,240 tokens. Do we have precedent for auto credits in these on-prem cases?
Priya S: We generally offer credits if we lost ingested events through our ingestion path (not caused by customer misconfig of agent). If the agent did drop on TTL because of customer's local retention, it's trickier. Document findings and tag legal + finance.
Kevin M: Update: broker logs show `recv seq=1422340` at 03:14:05 but with `checksum=bad` and then `drop silent` right after. Looks like the agent transmitted a corrupt payload during remount. I saved the raw packet capture to infra bucket (s3://redwood-debug/ventus/1799990123/pcap.gz).
Alex W: So agent thought it acked tokens but central dropped corrupted event -> billing mismatch. Customer still has the original event in their ledger?
Priya S: They do. They can re-export and we can re-ingest via a one-off ingestion job (non-production path) to reconcile billing. That means we'd bill for those tokens if re-ingested; but we should offer to credit since central dropped it.
Lisa B: Ok finance asks for a clean request: customer id, invoice window, token delta, and proposed credit amount. Alex, can you draft the reconciliation run plan + attach the pcap + ledger export?
Alex W: On it. Plan: request agent export for seq 1422340-43, validate checksums locally, run sanitized re-ingest with `--replay-force` flag (ops-only) to ensure idempotent apply, and mark central ledger with `source=onprem-replay-ventus-03`. Then issue a 18,240-token credit on invoice 2026-02-09. I'll include timeline and root cause (transient payload corruption during disk remount).
Kevin M: Also recommend we add an additional agent check: verify checksum before ack and delay ack until central confirms persist OR increase ack TTL for on-prem agents during maintenance windows. I'll open a runtime ticket.
Priya S: Good. Tagging @meter-agent-bot in the postmortem so we can surface metrics for `ack_ttl_expiry` trends across on-prem fleet.
meter-agent-bot: noted: created issue #INF-2147 ack_ttl_expiry trend analysis (priority=P2)
Alex W: I'll update the thread when export + pcap uploaded. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
